rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They fail to worship their Lord properly and show no kindness to people, not even by lending useful things whose owners retain and recover them.
rows.anchor: أي : لا أحسنوا عبادة ربهم ،   ولا أحسنوا إلى خلقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because they withhold even minor help, they are all the more likely to withhold zakat and other acts of devotion.
rows.anchor: فهؤلاء لمنع الزكاة وأنواع القربات أولى وأولى

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: Ali is reported to interpret al-ma'un as zakat.
rows.anchor: وقد قال ابن أبي نجيح عن مجاهد : قال علي : الماعون : الزكاة

rows.speaker: ابن عمر
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir says the interpretation of al-ma'un as zakat is also reported from Ibn Umar through several routes.
rows.anchor: وكذا روي من غير وجه عن ابن عمر

rows.speaker: محمد بن الحنفية، سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyya and Sa'id ibn Jubayr also identify al-ma'un with zakat.
rows.anchor: وبه يقول محمد بن الحنفية ،   وسعيد بن جبير

rows.speaker: عكرمة، مجاهد، عطاء، عطية العوفي
rows.claim: Ikrima, Mujahid, Ata, and Atiyya al-Awfi also identify al-ma'un with zakat.
rows.anchor: وعِكْرِمة ،   ومجاهد ،   وعطاء ،   وعطية العوفي

rows.speaker: الزهري، الحسن، قتادة، الضحاك، ابن زيد
rows.claim: Al-Zuhri, al-Hasan, Qatada, al-Dahhak, and Ibn Zayd also identify al-ma'un with zakat.
rows.anchor: والزهري ،   والحسن ،   وقتادة ،   والضحاك ،   وابن زيد

rows.speaker: الحسن البصري
rows.claim: Al-Hasan al-Basri describes a hypocrite who prays for show, feels no regret at missing prayer, and withholds the zakat or charity of his wealth.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن البصري : إن صلى راءى

rows.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
rows.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam says these are hypocrites: they perform the public prayer but deny the zakat that has been made obligatory.
rows.anchor: وقال زيد بن أسلم : هم المنافقون ظهرت الصلاة فصلوها

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
rows.claim: Abu al-Ubaydayn asked Ibn Masud, who defined al-ma'un as common loaned items such as an axe, pot, and bucket; two transmission routes give this answer.
rows.anchor: أن أبا العبيدين سأل عبد الله بن مسعود عن الماعون ،   فقال : هو ما يتعاوره الناس بينهم

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
rows.claim: A report through al-Masudi and Salama ibn Kuhayl repeats Ibn Masud's definition as items people lend one another, including an axe, pot, and bucket.
rows.anchor: عن أبي العُبَيدين : أنه سُئِل ابنُ مسعود عن الماعون ،   فقال : هو ما يتعاطاه

rows.speaker: أصحاب رسول الله
rows.claim: Ibn Masud reports that the Prophet's Companions used to say al-ma'un meant the bucket, axe, and pot, things one cannot do without.
rows.anchor: وسعد بن عياض ،   عن عبد الله

rows.speaker: أصحاب النبي
rows.claim: Sa'd ibn Iyad reports from the Prophet's Companions the same definition of al-ma'un as the loaned tools just mentioned.
rows.anchor: عن أبي إسحاق قال : سمعت سعد بن عياض يحدث عن أصحاب النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم مثله

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masud again defines al-ma'un as things people lend one another, such as an axe or bucket.
rows.anchor: عن عبد الله أنه سئل عن الماعون ،   فقال : ما يتعاوره الناس بينهم

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masud says that he and the Prophet's Companions called withholding a bucket and similar objects al-ma'un.
rows.anchor: عن أبي وائل ،   عن عبد الله قال : كنا مع نبينا صلى الله عليه وسلم ونحن نقول : الماعون

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
rows.claim: Abu Dawud and al-Nasa'i transmit Ibn Masud's saying that every good deed is charity and that al-ma'un in the Prophet's time meant lending a bucket and pot.
rows.anchor: ولفظ النسائي عن عبد الله قال : كل معروف صدقة ،   وكنا

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masud defines al-ma'un as borrowed household implements, including a pot, scales, and bucket.
rows.anchor: عن زر ،   عن عبد الله قال : الماعون : العواري : القدر

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas explains al-ma'un as household goods.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس : { وَيَمْنَعُونَ الْمَاعُونَ } يعني : متاع البيت

rows.speaker: مجاهد، إبراهيم النخعي، سعيد بن جبير، أبو مالك
rows.claim: Mujahid, Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, and Abu Malik define al-ma'un as lending household articles.
rows.anchor: وكذا قال مجاهد ،   وإبراهيم النخعي ،   وسعيد بن جبير ،   وأبو مالك

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A report from Ibn Abbas, transmitted through Mujahid, glosses the phrase as meaning that the owners have not yet arrived.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس : { وَيَمْنَعُونَ الْمَاعُونَ } قال : لم يجئ أهلها بعد

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas recounts three interpretations people held: withholding zakat, obedience, or loaned goods.
rows.anchor: وقال العوفي عن ابن عباس : { وَيَمْنَعُونَ الْمَاعُونَ } قال : اختلف الناس في ذلك

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: A report from Ali interprets al-ma'un as denying people the use of an axe, pot, or bucket.
rows.anchor: عن الحارث ،   عن علي : الماعون : منع الناس الفأس ،   والقدر ،   والدلو

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: Ikrima says the greatest instance of al-ma'un is zakat, while its least instances include a sieve, bucket, and needle.
rows.anchor: وقال عكرمة : رأس الماعون زكاة المال ،   وأدناه المنخل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir approves Ikrima's inclusive account: all interpretations return to withholding help through money or some benefit.
rows.anchor: وهذا الذي قاله عكرمة حسن ؛ فإنه يشمل الأقوال كلها

rows.speaker: محمد بن كعب
rows.claim: Muhammad ibn Ka'b glosses al-ma'un as recognized kindness or good conduct.
rows.anchor: ولهذا قال محمد بن كعب : { وَيَمْنَعُونَ الْمَاعُونَ } قال : المعروف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir invokes the hadith that every recognized good deed is charity.
rows.anchor: ولهذا جاء في الحديث : " كل معروف صدقة "

rows.speaker: الزهري
rows.claim: Al-Zuhri says that in Qurayshi usage al-ma'un means wealth.
rows.anchor: عن الزهري : { وَيَمْنَعُونَ الْمَاعُونَ } قال : بلسان قريش : المال

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A delegation report narrated by Qurra ibn Dam'us has the Prophet tell them not to withhold al-ma'un and identify it with water, metal and stone cooking pots, and iron tools such as their axe.
rows.anchor: قالوا : يا رسول الله ،   وما الماعون ؟ قال : " في الحجر ،   وفي الحديدة ،   وفي الماء "

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir calls the report very strange, rejects its Prophetic attribution as objectionable, and notes that its chain contains an unknown narrator.
rows.anchor: غريب جدا ،   ورفعه منكر ،   وفي إسناده من لا يعرف

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: Ibn al-Athir's Companion entry for Ali al-Namiri cites a report in which the Prophet says Muslims should return a greeting better and not withhold al-ma'un, which he explains as stone, iron, and similar things; Ibn Kathir gives no grading here.
rows.anchor: قلت : يا رسول الله ،   ما الماعون ؟ قال : " الحجر ،   والحديد ،   وأشباه ذلك "

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir identifies Sūrat al-Masad as a Meccan sūra.
rows.anchor:
تفسير سورة تبت
وهي مكية

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: In the Bukhari report from Ibn Abbas, the Prophet calls Quraysh to gather at al-Batha, asks whether they would believe a warning of an imminent enemy, and warns of severe punishment; Abu Lahab objects that this was why they were gathered, curses the Prophet, and the sūra is revealed.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس : أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم خرج إلى البطحاء

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: An alternate wording has Abu Lahab shake dust from his hands and say, 'Perish you all day; was this why you gathered us?' before the revelation.
rows.anchor: وفي رواية : فقام ينفض يديه ،   وهو يقول : تبا لك سائر اليوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir distinguishes the first phrase as a prayer against Abu Lahab and the second as a statement that his ruin has occurred.
rows.anchor: الأول : دعاء عليه ،   والثاني : خبر عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Lahab was the Prophet's paternal uncle, Abd al-Uzza ibn Abd al-Muttalib, also known by the kunya Abu Utba; he was nicknamed Abu Lahab for his shining face.
rows.anchor: واسمه : عبد العزى بن عبد المطلب ،   وكنيته أبو عتبة .   وإنما سمي " أبا لهب " لإشراق وجهه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir says Abu Lahab repeatedly harmed the Messenger, hated and scorned him, and belittled him and his religion.
rows.anchor: وكان كثير الأذية لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم والبغضة له

rows.speaker: ربيعة بن عباد الديلي
rows.claim: Rabi'a ibn Abbad recalls seeing the Prophet preach that affirming God's oneness brings success in the market of Dhu al-Majaz, while Abu Lahab followed him calling him a lying Sabi. Abu Lahab was handsome, squint-eyed, and wore two braids; people identified him as the Prophet's uncle.
rows.anchor: ربيعة بن عباد ،   من بني الديل ،   وكان جاهليًا فأسلم - قال : رأيت النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في الجاهلية في سوق ذي المجاز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir notes that Ahmad alone transmits this account; Rabi'a says he was not a child then, since he could already carry a waterskin.
rows.anchor: قال أبو الزناد : قلت لربيعة : كنت يومئذ صغيرًا ؟ قال : لا والله

rows.speaker: ربيعة بن عباد الديلي
rows.claim: In Ibn Ishaq's account reported by Rabi'a, the Prophet asks tribes to worship God alone, believe and protect him as he delivers God's message. Abu Lahab warns that the Prophet would make them abandon al-Lat, al-Uzza, and their allied jinn of Banu Malik ibn Uqays for innovation and misguidance, and urges them not to follow him. Ahmad and al-Tabarani also transmit this wording.
rows.anchor: سمعت ربيعة بن عباد الديلي يقول : إني لمع أبي رجل شاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir explains the first phrase as loss and failure, with Abu Lahab's deeds and efforts coming to nothing.
rows.anchor: فقوله تعالى : { تبت يدا أبي لهب } أي : خسرت وخابت ،   وضل عمله وسعيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second phrase confirms that Abu Lahab's ruin and destruction have indeed occurred.
rows.anchor: أي : وقد تب تحقق خسارته وهلاكه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وغيره
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas and other authorities understand 'what he earned' to mean Abu Lahab's children.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس وغيره : { وَمَا كَسَبَ } يعني : ولده

rows.speaker: عائشة، مجاهد، عطاء، الحسن، ابن سيرين
rows.claim: Aisha, Mujahid, Ata, al-Hasan, and Ibn Sirin are also reported to give the gloss 'his children.'
rows.anchor: وروي عن عائشة ،   ومجاهد ،   وعطاء ،   والحسن ،   وابن سيرين ،   مثله

words: مَآ أَغْنَىٰ عَنْهُ مَالُهُۥ وَمَا كَسَبَ
rows.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masud reports that when the Messenger called his people to faith, Abu Lahab said that if his nephew were truthful, he would ransom himself from punishment on Judgment Day with his wealth and children; the verse was then revealed.
rows.anchor: وذكر عن ابن مسعود أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لما دعا قومه إلى الإيمان ،   قال أبو لهب : إذا كان ما يقول ابن أخي حقا
